correctness.rationale: The classical integer digit maps hold at all boundaries with initial pair (1,0). The word 2, then q-1 zeros, then 2 maps every integer pair to (qx,qx), so disjoint block avoidance proves the arbitrary-modulus finite-level inequality without a limiting guess. The four nonzero opposite projective mod-three states cover all possibilities and produce exactly the displayed matrix, whose rational resolvent and Perron eigenvalue prove the exact formula and sharp exponent. Direct standalone integer testing produced VERIFY_OK 2251422; tests are corroboration, not a substitute for the complete proof.

value.rationale: The simultaneous all-modulus density-one result gives a natural profinite arithmetic distribution theorem for a classical restricted-partition sequence, not merely one congruence progression. The explicit ternary rational generating function, genuinely cubic Perron factor and optimal exponent for all cutoffs provide a meaningful exact prime-three refinement that the known parity result does not contain. Future studies of higher-modulus frequencies can build on the reset-word and projective-transfer structures.
